_comment: Phase 4. A breaker is open, which means a provider has been taken out of
rotation and traffic is being refused before it leaves this process.
The failure rate is the more informative number and it is the wrong one to
alert on. It reports -1 below minimumCalls - 'not enough calls to judge',
which is a different thing from 0% - and CircuitBreakerMetrics maps that to
NaN so it graphs as a gap rather than as a healthy provider. NaN is dropped
by the OTLP exporter, so the series is simply absent whenever the breaker is
idle, and an alert on an absent series is an alert that cannot fire.
state is 0 closed / 1 open / 2 half-open, always present, and says the thing
an operator actually needs to know.
matchType 1 is 'at least once'. mockpsp's waitInOpenSeconds is 10, so a
breaker can open, half-open and reclose well inside one evaluation - 'all
the time' would miss exactly the incident this is for.

annotations.description: The breaker for {{$labels.psp}}:{{$labels.operation}} is not closed (0=closed, 1=open, 2=half-open). Calls are being refused locally and the provider is receiving no traffic for this operation.
